transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Time: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Astra - Head of Platform), Owen Reyes (Astra - Security Engineer), Priya Kapoor (Astra - PM)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on data handling and retention controls: request storage toggles, logging redaction, PII detection, console settings, and what Dedicated/Private options look like for Astra's compliance needs. Customer asked for SOC2/ISO artifacts, encryption/KMS details, and an initial pricing estimate for a 3-month pilot.

Topics covered:
- Data retention toggles (request storage on/off)
- Automated PII redaction and regex masking
- Console demo: audit logs, per-route retention policies
- API flags for immediate redaction and ephemeral requests
- Dedicated vs Hosted considerations for e2e encryption, KMS/HSM integration
- Redwood Optimize (misheard as Redwood-Optima by customer) suggestions to reduce logging volume

Transcript:
[00:00] Speaker 1 (Lena): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate Astra taking the time. Today Samir and I will walk through our data handling controls — logging redaction, request storage toggles, and a few console features. Should be about 30-45 minutes, leave time for Q&A.
[00:20] Speaker 2 (Maya): Thanks Lena. Quick context: we're evaluating how Redwood would fit into our payments stack. Primary concerns are PII leakage, retention windows for transactions, and auditability for regulators.
[00:35] Speaker 1 (Lena): Totally, that's what we want to focus on. Samir, do you want to take the console demo?
[00:40] Speaker 3 (Samir): Yeah, jumping in. I'm sharing my screen — let me know if you can't see it. Ok, this is the Redwood Console, top nav shows API, Models, Console, Optimize. I'm opening the project for Astra-demo.
[01:05] Speaker 2 (Owen): I'm seeing it. Can you jump to the security section first?
[01:10] Speaker 3 (Samir): Sure. Under Settings -> Data & Retention we have toggles for "Request storage" which is the big one. By default hosted requests are stored for 30 days for debugging and billing, but you can flip Request Storage off for an org or per-route.
[01:30] Speaker 4 (Priya): Per-route? So we could keep logs for some non-sensitive routes and turn off others?
[01:35] Speaker 3 (Samir): Exactly. You can set retention policy per route — e.g., /internal-summary keeps 90 days, /payment-card only has storage disabled, or set to ephemeral for 0 days.
[01:50] Speaker 2 (Maya): How does that interact with streaming responses? If we stream tokens, are they stored?
[01:57] Speaker 3 (Samir): Good question — streaming is handled as events. If Request Storage is off at the route level, we don't persist full payloads. We keep only the minimal metadata for tracing (request id, timestamp) for a limited period (configurable), unless you enable debug snapshots. There is also an API-level flag you can pass: x-redwood-request-storage: false to force ephemeral for that call.
[02:20] Speaker 2 (Owen): Does that mean we can set it at runtime from our services? That's important for PCI-sensitive flows.
[02:27] Speaker 3 (Samir): Yes, you can control it from the API call — sdk or REST header — so your app can route certain flows as ephemeral.
[02:35] Speaker 2 (Owen): Ok good. What about PII detection and redaction? We need to make sure card numbers, SSNs are never written to logs.
[02:43] Speaker 3 (Samir): We have two layers: automatic PII detectors and deterministic redaction rules. The automatic detectors run a classification model to identify likely PII (card numbers, SSN, emails). By default we mask those values in logs and transcripts. You can also configure custom redaction rules: regex patterns, named groups, or structured keys for json payloads.
[03:05] Speaker 4 (Priya): Can we supply our own regex patterns?
[03:08] Speaker 3 (Samir): Yes, per org or per project. For example, many finance customers supply a PCI regex we apply before storage. Also you can configure an allowlist so certain non-sensitive paths bypass the detector.
[03:20] Speaker 2 (Maya): How reliable is the detector? We can't rely solely on heuristics for compliance audits.
[03:26] Speaker 3 (Samir): It's high-precision but not perfect — we recommend defense-in-depth: use Request Storage off for sensitive routes, supply regex rules for PCI tokens, and integrate client-side redaction where possible. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can integrate with your DLP tooling for in-transit masking.
[03:45] Speaker 1 (Lena): Also worth noting: we keep audit logs that show who toggled retention settings and when. Those are independent and not removed by request storage turning off —audit entries are minimal and store metadata about config changes, required for compliance.
[04:05] Speaker 2 (Owen): Are audit logs part of SOC 2 export? And are they encrypted with KMS?
[04:10] Speaker 1 (Lena): Yes, audit logs are available for export and are encrypted. For Private/Dedicated we integrate with your KMS/HSM. For hosted we offer customer-managed KMS via cloud KMS integrations.
[04:22] Speaker 2 (Owen): If we run a Private deploy, does Redwood maintain any copies? We need to know about data residency.
[04:29] Speaker 3 (Samir): In a Private on-prem deployment, control plane can run in your VPC with no data plane egress. We can configure retention to your policy and we don't keep copies outside your environment unless specifically configured. For Dedicated we still operate the control plane but we can restrict region and set retention to 0 for request payloads.
[04:50] Speaker 4 (Priya): Can you show an example of a per-route policy?
[04:55] Speaker 3 (Samir): Yep. Back to the console -> Routes -> /api/v1/processPayment -> Policy. Here you can see Request Storage: Off, Redaction rules: PCI regex (custom), PII detection: Enabled (masking), Retention window: 0 days. There's also a toggle for "store request metadata only" which keeps request id and status but not the full body.
[05:22] Speaker 2 (Maya): And how about logs we already ingested? If we change a policy to off, will prior logs be deleted?
[05:30] Speaker 3 (Samir): We support a "purge" operation. If you switch to off and request a purge, we will delete stored payloads in accordance with your request. Purge requests are logged in the audit trail and we provide a job id for the purge operation. There are legal safeguards — for example, we require an admin SSO confirmation step to avoid accidental deletes.
[05:50] Speaker 2 (Owen): That admin confirmation is good. For PCI we'll also need an immutable record of who requested a purge.
[05:58] Speaker 1 (Lena): That's exactly what the audit log contains — actor, timestamp, job id.
[06:05] Speaker 4 (Priya): What about embeddings and logs containing derivatives? If we generate embeddings from user data, does that fall under request storage?
[06:15] Speaker 3 (Samir): Embeddings are stored separately. We have retention settings for embedding stores too — you can set embeddings to ephemeral or to a named vector-db managed by your account. For sensitive data we recommend ephemeral embeddings or encrypting the vector store.
[06:30] Speaker 2 (Maya): Do you offer customer-managed encryption for those stores?
[06:34] Speaker 3 (Samir): Yes, same KMS integrations apply — you can manage keys for both payload and embedding storage.
[06:40] Speaker 2 (Owen): Regarding the API, you mentioned a header. Is there an SDK method as well?
[06:45] Speaker 3 (Samir): Yes, both. SDKs in our supported languages have a requestStorage=false parameter and an ephemeral flag. We also expose a console API if you want to programmatically update retention policies.
[07:00] Speaker 2 (Maya): Can you demo the API call?
[07:04] Speaker 3 (Samir): Sure — quick example: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "x-redwood-request-storage: false" -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate. That will mark that request as ephemeral. The header is case-insensitive.
[07:26] Speaker 2 (Owen): For high-throughput flows, will toggling to ephemeral affect performance?
[07:32] Speaker 3 (Samir): Very minimal. Storage is orthogonal to the inference path; the major cost is network and serving. Disabling storage just skips a persistence step. On Dedicated we can even route ephemeral requests to a faster hot path since we don't need to snapshot payloads.
[07:50] Speaker 1 (Lena): Also want to call out Redwood Optimize suggestions — it will flag high-volume routes and propose batching or cache suggestions which indirectly reduce logging surface. (small laugh) Samir: yep Redwood Optimize (customer misheard earlier) will propose trimming context and caching prefixes to lower both cost and stored payload volume.
[08:10] Speaker 4 (Priya): How do we get the SOC2 artifacts?
[08:14] Speaker 1 (Lena): I'll share the security pack after the call. It includes SOC 2 type II attestation, ISO docs, data retention whitepaper, and our KMS/HSM integration guide.
[08:22] Speaker 2 (Maya): Great. Anything about legal holds? If a regulator demands we preserve certain logs, can we override retention?
[08:30] Speaker 3 (Samir): We support legal holds: you can set an org-level legal hold that prevents purges for specific ids or date ranges. That is recorded and only removable by authorized admins.
[08:44] Speaker 2 (Owen): For our Compliance team, we'll want a runbook for producing artifacts for audits. Can you generate exports in CSV/JSON?
[08:52] Speaker 3 (Samir): Yes. Audit exports are available via the console and API. They include filtered payloads per policy and metadata. For sensitive payloads, we can export masked versions and provide proof of masking for the audit.
[09:10] Speaker 4 (Priya): One thing — do you keep any telemetry in logs by default that could be considered PII? IP addresses, user ids?
[09:18] Speaker 3 (Samir): By default we capture minimal metadata — request id, route, region, latency. IP collection is configurable; we can disable or hash IPs on ingest. User identifiers are subject to your redaction rules.
[09:32] Speaker 2 (Maya): Will you support SSO for admin controls and can we enforce MFA?
[09:37] Speaker 1 (Lena): Yes SSO (SAML/SCIM) is supported with enforced MFA options. RBAC: you can create roles (admin, security, devops) and restrict purge permissions to a small group.
[09:48] Speaker 2 (Owen): Good. For our pilot, we want to run a small Dedicated cluster in us-east-1 with request storage off for payment routes, and run benchmarks.
[09:58] Speaker 1 (Lena): That's a common approach. We'll propose a 3-month pilot: dedicated GPU pool + network isolation, request storage off for payment routes, SOC2 review. We'll give a price estimate after we know LE (load estimate).
[10:12] Speaker 4 (Priya): Timing: we're hoping to have vendor selected by end of Oct, pilot run in Nov. Is that workable?
[10:18] Speaker 1 (Lena): Yes, timeline looks reasonable. Next steps: I'll send security docs, Samir will send sandbox token + demo script, and we'll schedule a POC kickoff.
[10:30] Speaker 2 (Maya): One more question — do you have per-tenant encryption at rest by default?
[10:36] Speaker 3 (Samir): Yes, all stored data is encrypted at rest. For customer-managed keys we use cloud KMS. For Private we can integrate with HSM.
[10:45] Speaker 2 (Owen): Any limitation around key rotation and access logs?
[10:49] Speaker 3 (Samir): We support key rotation and we log key usage in an audit trail. Those logs are part of the security export but key material is never exported.
[10:58] Speaker 1 (Lena): Great, I'm going to open the Q&A bucket now — any other specific concerns?
[11:05] Speaker 4 (Priya): Latency vs storage: if we enable extra redaction steps will that add to request latency?
[11:10] Speaker 3 (Samir): Minimal. Redaction runs on the persistence path, not the critical token generation path. For most customers redaction adds under 10ms on the persistence side. If you do synchronous redaction pre-inference that's different — we usually recommend async or persistence-time redaction.
[11:28] Speaker 2 (Maya): If we need synchronous redaction pre-inference for regulatory reasons, will that require a Private deploy?
[11:36] Speaker 3 (Samir): Possibly — Private gives you more control for in-line DLP integration. We can discuss architecture patterns in the POC.
[11:45] Speaker 1 (Lena): Alright we are at about 40 minutes — quick recap?
[11:50] Speaker 3 (Samir): Recap: 1) Request Storage toggles per route + API header for ephemeral calls. 2) PII detection + custom regex redaction. 3) Audit logs & purge job with admin confirmation. 4) KMS/HSM integration, customer-managed keys, and Private/Dedicated deployment options. 5) Next steps: security pack, sandbox, pricing for 3-month Dedicated pilot.
[12:20] Speaker 2 (Maya): Sounds good, thanks both.
[12:25] Speaker 4 (Priya): Thank you.
[12:27] Speaker 1 (Lena): We'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the POC kick off. Thanks everyone.
